incidents.summary: A customer who required ankle surgery after slipping on spilled coconut oil at Sainsbury’s sued the company, alleging staff negligently failed to identify and clear the spill.

sources.title: Sainsbury's Sued for £500,000 after Coconut Oil Accident - HSE People
sources.quote: Legal secretary Georgina Hennessy slipped on a ‘spilt coconut oil product’ in a branch of Sainsbury’s in July 2019, resulting in a broken ankle and being left bleeding on the floor.

sources.title: Sainsbury's Sued for £500,000 after Coconut Oil Accident - HSE People
sources.quote: Ms Hennessy had to undergo an operation to have a metal plate and screws inserted into her ankle.

sources.title: Sainsbury's Sued for £500,000 after Coconut Oil Accident - HSE People
sources.quote: Ms Hennessy is now suing J Sainsbury Plc for up to £500,000 at the High Court, claiming store staff negligently failed to spot and clear up the mess.

incidents.summary: Sainsbury’s faced a ShareAction-backed investor campaign to obtain Living Wage Foundation accreditation and extend real living wage pay to subcontracted workers.

sources.title: Sainsbury's pressed to pay more to subcontracted workers - BBC
sources.quote: But some investors are calling for it to sign up to the Living Wage Foundation's pay commitments.

sources.title: Sainsbury's pressed to pay more to subcontracted workers - BBC
sources.quote: If it does, the higher pay rate would be extended to subcontracted staff, such as cleaners.

sources.title: Sainsbury's pressed to pay more to subcontracted workers - BBC
sources.quote: ShareAction, the group behind the campaign for a new pay policy at the supermarket, said there was a "compelling moral case" for offering all staff, including subcontracted workers, the higher rate.

positives: Sainsbury’s paid its direct employees above the Living Wage Foundation’s real living wage rate.
